Lead times are highly variable (CV=0.715, range 0.38-4.73 days), necessitating a robust safety stock of 3,473 units at the 95% service level. The EOQ-derived order quantity of 20,440 is capped at 12,760 by the storage constraint of 16,233 units; this binding cap is flagged. The recommended (r,Q) policy consolidates orders from ~143 to ~41 per year, cutting total annual costs by 54%.

research_insights.selection_rationale: The high non-zero demand fraction (96.5%) and large daily volumes make continuous review appropriate. Fixed order quantity Q simplifies procurement and captures EOQ savings. The bimodal pattern is handled by a generous safety stock rather than periodic review, which would require larger pipeline buffers.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap binds hard: the unconstrained EOQ (20,440) exceeds available space after safety stock reservation (12,760 units remaining). This reduces average cycle stock and increases ordering frequency vs. the unconstrained optimum, adding ~$200/year in ordering costs. If storage can be expanded, the full EOQ would save an additional ~$200/year.
